info_text: Shopping Center Arcade in São Paulo. / HotZone is a Brazilian arcade chain that mixes classic arcade games—with newer attractions such as VR rides and 4D cinema experiences. / This particular location is on the ground floor of MorumbiShopping, close to Exit C. It actually takes up several store units, and you can enter directly through Entrance C. Despite the large space, it’s usually very crowded, which says a lot about how popular it is. The arcade is air-conditioned, so at least you won’t melt while playing. / HotZone doesn’t sell food or drinks inside, but you’re allowed to bring your own, which is a big plus. The arcade runs on a card-based balance system: you load credits onto a card using cash or credit/debit cards (Visa and Mastercard are accepted). Any balance you add is valid for 180 days from the last time you use it. / If you recharge R$100 or more at once, you get VIP status. This gives you a 25% discount from Monday to Friday, and 15% off on weekends and holidays—pretty solid if you go often. / There are two types of credits: Normal and Bonus. Machines that only accept Normal credits have a pink-glowing card reader, while machines that accept both Normal and Bonus...

Alongside the arcade, there's bowling, redemption games, a driving sim, VR, and axe throwing. / It uses a card system, though the cards are smaller and can be attached to a bracelet-like strap. As of mid-2019, they have transitioned to a different vendor for the cards (you can exchange them for free). info_text: This place is now "Toy Box Cranes" and mostly has claw machines. FUNtime card still works here. / --- / FUNtime is an arcade at the Pacific Mall that caters to kids. It launched as the Playscape arcade by Cineplex (Player One Amusement Group, formerly Playdium), and it used to be a decent place for all ages to enjoy music games: Dance Dance Revolution, In The Groove, DrumMania and more. The arcade, like many owned by Cineplex, started to decline since 2009. In 2016, Cineplex converted it to FUNtime, to the ire of Green Tea and over 1,300 other gamers. FUNtime retained a pair of Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune 3 racers momentarily, but as of 2018, these have been removed. info_text: You can reach the mall by taking the train to Gare Saint-Laurent-du Var and walk around 10 minutes. / The arcade is located on the south side of the CAP 3000 mall. Enter the mall from the south entrance, there you can ask the reception desk for directions. Take the escalator 1 floor up and walk west, you'll find the arcade where there's a lot of blue lights. / This arcade does not use physical coins as credits, instead they use cards for buying and spending credits. You can look for the yellow machines and purchase/top-up credits, then you will receive a card (for free) to this arcade containing credits. The credits are not refundable and the card is permanent, meaning that you don't have to return it. Touch the card on the arcade machines to pay credits, then the corresponding amount is automatically deducted from your card.

Truism is rising at this area any many new resorts (and arcades) are in local area. / ===2014=== / The pier is impossible to miss, as it's one of the focal points of this seaside resort. / It was rebuilt on the site of the old pier, in 1994. / The day I went in September the top part of the arcade (Salon Joker, a famous chain in Poland) was open, yet the downstairs with EZ2, DDR and Pump was shut due to off season. I saw the cabinets through the padlocked gate, which was very irritating! / The arcade in general is well maintained and very clean. / There is another makeshift arcade with Tekken, Need for Speed and Virtua Fighter next to a bumper cars setup further inland. The village itself is very nice (in the summer) with a Poland "Hollywood walk of fame" style boulevard and the beach is sandy, clean, and goes out for miles. It's kind of isola...

info_text: Sports hall that also has an NX2. / "Miejski Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji is located in a calm area of Kołobrzeg, 800 metres from the boulevard on the Parsęta River. It offers rooms with free Wi-Fi and a TV, as well as free access to the aqua park and 1 gym ticket. The rooms of the Miejscki Ośrodek feature a classic, elegant interior design and are painted in warm pastel colours. Each one has a seating area, work desk and a spacious private bathroom. While staying at the Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji you can work out at the gym, take a swim in the indoor swimming pool, or play a game of tennis. The spa and wellness centre provides various treatments. The Millenium restaurant specialises in Polish cuisine, in the morning breakfast is served here. Kołobrzeg’s city centre is within 1 km. The city’s main railway station is 1.4 km away. The beach on the Baltic sea is within 2.2 km. Free parking is provided. / Read more: http://www.lonelyplanet.com/poland/kolobrzeg/hotels/miejski-osrodek-sportu-i-rekreacji#ixzz2eZYXTCM8".

info_text: To get to Lotte World find your way to Jamsil Station on Line 2 or 8. Follow the many signs to the park. Admission is cheaper with a Shinhan bank card. / Lotte World is a huge Korean theme park, perhaps the best. It is a knock off of the Disney Parks but it is pretty cool on its own merit. It is the world's largest indoor theme park (and it is indeed impressive). There are a ton of good rides here, Atlantis Adventure, Cosmic Express, Pharoah's Fury and Gyro Swing were my favorites. / The arcade locations are all located in the indoor park. The is one arcade, the Moroccan arcade, with a lot of fighting games (Tekken 6 etc.) The arcade with rhythm games was located next to the "Happy Tree Picnic" ride, and "Marion Crepes". It is on the first floor. There is another arcade on floor three by the big loop of "French Revolution" with nothing of interest. There is one more arcade connected to the Folk Museum apparently, but I did not have a chance to explore. / Overall it's a great park, I expected a lot more rhythm games though. Maybe they are hidden somewhere...

info_text: Associació A.R.C.A.D.E. (aka ARCADE.cat) is a non-profit cultural association aiming the preservation and divulgation of arcade games and culture, by a wide array of means: collaborating with cultural entities and other media such as films, podcasts, radios, etc, organizing tournaments, and restoring machines of its private collection. Our main objective is to preserve the feel and essence of old arcades, as well as modern ones. / The association is run collaboratively by its members in their free time as a labor of love, with frequent events, workshops and tournaments. Its premises is home to an extensive collaborative collection of arcade and pinball machines that cover over 40+ years of arcade history. It has a mix of dedicated cabinets (rhythm games, racing games, classic games, etc.) as well as Candy cabinets and Spanish generic cabinets from the 90s, with games usually being switched from time to time. All of them are set on Free To Play. / Keep in mind, this is not a game center open to the public. Access to the premises is for members and accompanying guests only. However, we hold many different tournaments throughout the year (A.R.C., SHMUPFEST, TBAP and more upcoming)...

info_text: La industria de los videojuegos diseñados para salones recreativos, dejó de estar presente en Europa a finales del año 2000. Los videojuegos domésticos de nueva generación, los impuestos abusivos, y la crisis hizo que las maquinas recreativas dejaran de fabricarse, y lo más grave… que estos sistemas fueran destruidos para no pagar las tasas mensuales que sus propietarios debían abonar sólo por tenerlas. / En Arcade Planet, hemos conseguido rescatar y restaurar las mejores recreativas de la historia, y preservando los mejores juegos de todos los sistemas. / Arcade Planet ofrece su increíble colección de Arcades para eventos, exposiciones, organización de torneos, y sesiones de juego libre “free play”. / Con esta iniciativa aquellos que jugaron en los 80 y 90 volverán a recordar los mejores ratos de ocio de sus vidas… y las nuevas generaciones descubrirán la especial interpretación del modo de juego creado para salones recreativos… donde el único propósito es la diversión inmediata. / (PLEASE CHECK OPENING TIMES ON EITHER FACEBOOK OR INSTAGRAM, BETWEEN 15:00 AND 17:00 THERE'S A PAUSE AND THE ARCADE CLOSES THOSE 2 HOURS). / The out of order board was the same as Litwak’s Arcade. info_text: Nextage is a non-profit association in Madrid and the meeting point for the largest rhythm game communities in Spain. This is where fans of Pump It Up (PIU), ITG, DDR, Sound Voltex, and Beatmania IIDX live, with tournaments, challenges, and meetups in a close, authentic environment. We're not a business: we're a community built by and for arcade lovers. If you're looking to improve, enjoy, or simply share this hobby with people like you, this is your place. / Access to the warehouse is for members and accompanying guests. You can also appoint a visit on the open days at weekends on their website. / Entrance fee is 7€ (or 10€ for both weekend days), and you can become a member for 30€/month, which includes entry into a private group, and being able to come on weekdays / If you'd like more information on the project or would like to arrange for a visit, please contact at our social media.

info_text: Billiards, games and GREAT food. THAT'S what Eight On The Break is all about! 3 Brunswick Gold Crown Regulation Tables, over 50 great games (classic and new) and some of the best playing pinballs ANYWHERE! / For 50 years we have provided the Northern New Jersey area with the best in family entertainment. / Please come and enjoy "The Break" I think you will find this unusual different family fun center has everything you could ever want. / The Story: / Eight On the Break was founded by Edward Montross in 1973. Ed was WAY far ahead of his time. Many years later a new generation (me) would take his concept and run with it! info_text: The traditional pizza rat experience! Lots of low-value ticket games, kids high as your knees running around every which way, a salad bar that you don't want to touch unless you're looking to develop new and undiscovered diseases, an underpaid teenager walking around in the mascot costume for five minutes on the hour every hour. Now with brand new "2.0" experiences like a large TV instead of animatronics, a digital dancefloor, a trampoline zone, and a mini ninja warrior course. Oh yeah, and some of the blandest undercooked pizza you'll ever taste in your life, with what feels like a pound of salt dumped directly on top. It's Chuck E. Cheese, where a kid can be a kid! / All games here take game cards, which either can be loaded with points or time play. The only exception is the giant claw machine, which only takes money or credit cards.

Although the mall officially opens at 10 AM, D&B does not open their doors to the public until 11 AM except during their special summer hours, when they open one hour earlier than posted. / There is a 18 year old age minimum requirement because they serve alcohol. However, up to four underage patrons are permitted per one 25+ year old adult. This sometimes may vary depending on whether or not a bouncer is present. Bouncers do not usually appear until after 6 PM nowadays. / Most of the games here take D&B Power Cards (with a few exceptions). You can either purchase them from the counter near the main entrance, or from any of the self-serve kiosks spread throughout the area. Games themselves cost "chips"; 1 chip is equivalent to costing 20¢ by default when loading $20 on a Power Card, but you can lower that per-chip cost by buying in bulk and/or utilizing specia...

info_text: The Family Fun Center is a family-owned arcade located at the York Galleria mall on the upstairs level between Boscov’s and the food court. Its history dates back 40 years with its previous tenure at the now defunct Harrisburg East Mall. It was famous for hosting ITG tournaments throughout the years in Harrisburg, with the cab now at the present York location and still maintained by the community. They also have a Betson DDR SuperNova 2, an American DDR X cab, and a Guitar Hero arcade cab. Games are a dollar or below. Games range from 1980s-today. / Hours posted differ from the rest of the mall's hours, so I decided to post them here. / Website: https://www.yorkfamilyfun.com / 1 Token = 25¢. info_text: Arcade contains an assortment of 80s arcade games and pinball as well as modern titles from the 90s/00s. Games are grouped by their genre, so similar games should be located close to each other unless otherwise noted. The pinball machines are typically turned off; most of the tables (except for newer games) can be turned on via a switch under the right leg of the table. The attendant at the front should make you aware of this. / Entry into the arcade is $15; there is an ATM inside the entrance (with transaction fees, of course). Air hockey, claw machines, and a few games in the arcade cost extra. Food, drinks, and candy are also sold in the facility with tables and chairs provided. There's also a party room available for rent. / Editors Note: Games listed as "Unknown" condition in the list are working but untested, unless otherwise noted. info_text: Massive tri-level arcade and family entertainment center inside of a gigantic castle located in Nashua, NH, just over the Massachusetts state line. The first floor is mostly redemption games and kid's games, and also features a reasonably priced snack bar. The second floor has modern arcade games alongside classics and rarities from the 90's and 2000's, as well as three rides including a double-decker carousel, Himalaya, and roller coaster. The third floor is currently more sparsely populated but contains a small selection of pinball machines and rhythm games. / All games operate via tokens. Tokens can be purchased with cash at any of the change machines located throughout the building, or with credit cards at the front counter. Each $20 purchased will give you a bonus $5 worth of tokens. The only things that do not operate with tokens are the rides; tickets for these can be purchased at the front counter, excluding the roller coaster which is removed and will be replaced with the Gemstone Mining attraction. / This arcade opens with limited hours from Fridays-Sundays during the school year and Wednesdays-Sundays during school vacations and summer.

info_text: Game Galaxy's sole location. It contains hundreds of arcade games and pinball tables neatly organized. A few Laserdisc and vector games are present at the location but are only playable on Saturdays. The place also has consoles to play at the front of the store, including consoles for fighting games, Super Smash Bros. Melee, retro titles, and a PSVR setup. There are some Nintendo Switch Taiko games and two controllers, but you'll have to set those up yourself. / [b]IMPORTANT:[/b] Some sections of games may be turned off to save energy. If a game is off when you visit (and it does not have an "out of order" sign), ask the staff at the front desk to turn them on. Most pinball machines are off but can be turned on by flipping a switch under the right leg. / Some newer pinball tables require quarters to play in addition to entry; prices are noted on this list and on the machines. There is the $25 premium rate you can pay at entry to play these tables at no extra charge. / Canned drinks and snacks may be purchased from the front desk. Soft drink cans are $2, water bottles are $1, and 8.5oz Red Bulls are $4. Selection of drinks vary. / This listing is by no means complete or accurate...

There is a metered parking lot behind the arcade near Kaiser Permanente, with a walkway between it and the front entrance. / [i]History:[/i] High Scores Arcade is a privately owned "interactive spite arcade museum" opened in August 2010 by Shawn and Meg Livernoche. They once had a location in Hayward, CA, but they closed it down because of the COVID-19 pandemic and later opened [url=https://zenius-i-vanisher.com/v5.2/arcade.php?id=7406]another location in Monterey[/url]. info_text: This arcade is a part of Ocean Beach. This means that you have to pay to park to go to the arcade, unless you can get dropped off or walk there. Their official listed hours online are on weekends only, from 11 AM to 5 PM each day, but they may be open outside of those hours during the summer season depending upon foot traffic. They also run the amusement park and water slide inside of Ocean Beach Park. / All games in this arcade take tokens, and the redemption games spit out paper tickets. There are change machines located next to both main entrances, as well as in the middle of the arcade. During a recent June 2025 visit, many games were unplugged and out of order, as they appeared to be in the process of reorganizing the layout. However, the owner Lindsey was happy to try and get some of the OOO games playable for us by request. If there are any issues with the games, please notify one of the members of the staff, as they will do their best to get things up and running for you, and if not possible, refund your tokens.

info_text: Massive retro arcade and pinball museum located in Girard, Ohio inside of a former grocery store. The owner, Rob Berk, is the current Guinness World Record holder for the world's largest pinball machine collection with over 1000 machines in his collection, of which over 400 of them are currently out on the floor and playable. Also includes over 200 other arcade games from throughout the years, including a mix of classic electro-mechanical machines, retro video games from the 70's through 90's, and a small amount of more modern games. All games, excluding redemption games and display pieces, are set to free play. / One flat fee for entry. Current pricing as of May 2025 is as follows; / $20 - adults (16+) / $10 - kids (6-15) / Free - "little ones" (5 and younger) / They also offer memberships at various rates for periods of 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year. Also offered is a lifetime membership for adults. More details on these memberships are available on their website.

info_text: Located on the 2nd floor of the Deptford Mall in the space formerly occupied by Sears, this Round1 location features a wide variety of rhythm game favorites alongside other popular arcade and redemption games, over 50 crane machines, a bowling alley, 5 pool tables, a food service counter and bar, and two large karaoke rooms. This location does not contain any darts, ping pong tables, or Spo-Cha. As of July 2026, they have also added a small selection of pinball machines, and vastly expanded the selection of claw machines. / There are two entrances; The first is from the outside door, which you take an escalator or elevator up. The other one is from the second floor of the mall. / The rhythm game section has been moved to the area next to the party rooms (on the escalator side of the arcade). The area near the mall entrance that formerly had rhythm games is now home to dual screen racers, VR games, and coin pushers. / Pricing is the same as other R1 locations throughout the US, and all the usual house rules apply with regards to patrons under 18.

There are a couple of options available, visit the front counter for more information. / Most music games are 8.4 credits per play. Some of the machines are louder than others, but many of them are equipped with headphone jacks, so be sure to bring along a pair of headphones with a long enough cord just in case games around you are too loud. / Water bottles are allowed! If you are bringing in an open container, security may ask to verify that the bottle does not contain alcohol. The easiest thing to do would be to bring in an empty bottle, and fill it up with water at the drinking fountains upstairs near the bathrooms. You can also purchase bottled water at the concession stand for $2.50, and refill the bottle as many times as you like. / Late at night during the weekends, security may ask to see your ID to verify your age before you are able to enter the arcade. Staff and security may also be a bit pushy when closing time is near. Outdoor attractions include go-karts, a zip line, two 18-hole mini golf courses, and a selection of rides such as bumper cars and a kiddie roller coaster. Indoor attractions include an inflatable obstacle park, laser tag, a laser maze, a rock climbing wall, axe throwing, and a decent sized arcade with a mixed variety of different games. / All arcade games operate via card swipers. info_text: From the website: / What is The Forge? / The Forge is a Social Gaming Center, also known as a gaming lounge or e-sports lounge. It is a dedicated space where gamers can come together to play their favorite video games. We provide a unique experience for gamers, offering high-end equipment, comfortable seating, and food and beverage options. We try to foster a social and community atmosphere, allowing gamers to compete in tournaments, form their own communities, and engage in social interactions. / The Forge is not limited to just console or PC games. We also encompass online gaming platforms where people can both play and watch others play. We also encourage tabletop gaming, from Warhammer to Monopoly. Our community includes features such as a dedicated Discord server, activity feeds, leaderboards, and shareable content. We cater to a diverse audience from all walks of life, from casual gamers who enjoy single-player games to competitive gamers who participate in multiplayer games and tournaments. The Forge aims to become a significant part of the gaming culture in Tampa Bay, providing a platform for gamers to connect, compete, and share their gaming experiences. / Here at The F...

info_text: Formerly Free Play Arlington. / Tokyo Station has two primary game zones: / Free Play Tokyo: Purchase an optional $11 day-pass wristband and gain access 55+ Japanese imports all set to our favorite game setting of all time: “Free Play”. This zone is built for exploration and features: (1) an ever-changing selection of Japanese fighters, puzzle games, and more in classic Japanese “candy” arcade cabinets, (2) a curated selection of the most sought after Japanese rhythm games, (3) imported racing games, (4) a selection of Japanese releases in their classic American wooden cabs (think Galaga), and (5) revolving bonus arcade content. / Tokyo Station: You’re not in Tokyo if your arcade doesn’t have an incredible selection of prized skill games! Expect a massive selection of custom claw games featuring the most authentic Japanese prize selection available in the USA along with a wall of imported Gachapon from the largest independent importer of Japanese capsule toys (that’s us!) info_text: Astro City is located on the second floor overlooking the High Street and Southchurch Road. After you get to the top of the stairs, you'll enter a small room with a number of arcade machines. Go through the door on the left to the end of the corridor and you'll find the main arcade area. Continue to the left, past the snack bar and you'll arrive at the new food area. / PUBLIC OPENING / Public opening is now restricted to various two and three hour sessions throughout the week. There's a complete list of session times on our website, just click on "Free Play Sessions" on the drop down. As of 19/12/18 there are 56 machines and games set to free play and entry is only £5 per person. / PRIVATE PARTIES / All other times are reserved for private children's birthday parties and adult arcade hire. / FACILITIES / Toilets, snack/coffee bar and a food eating area. / OTHER MACHINES / Astro City has a large number of machines, games and rides that do not feature in the main list. info_text: Typical bowling alley arcade, sadly most of the focus is on redemption games but there are a handful of actual video games to play. It's all quite modern which is actually pretty great, unless of course you're looking for something retro. Most games, bar the Dancing Stage EuroMIX cab, are kept to a really great condition, prices are generally £1 a go, a couple of the bigger machines being £2. / Crowd wise you can often find a lot of kids but they're harmless. Good area for Streetpassing on your Nintendo 3DS! Since Hollywood Bowl is in a leisure park you have a few other attractions such as Odeon, a multitude of places to eat including Nandos, McDonalds, KFC, Pizza Hut, Coast II Coast, Chiquitos, ASK and a couple others I'm forgetting. There is a club nearby called Chicago's which gets very busy on Thursday nights as that is the student night, however I daresay they'd not waste their time in a sub-par arcade over a nightclub haha. / Website says the place is open from 10:00 "til late", I'm not certain what time that means.

address: 110-114 Harbour Parade Ramsgate Kent, CT11 8LP , Ramsgate
info_text: "As I drove past Merlins to that corner by the Rose and Crown that we all love to see, I noticed the 'Mr B's' arcades had been turned into a 'Jimmy G's' instead. Jimmy Godden has bought both sides of Mr B's, both phase I and II. The larger of the two, phase II, has been completely renovated giving it a more modern look. The roof has been completely torn down and replaced, which must have cost one hell of a lot as I know it to have had an asbestos problem, and could not be touched. I was especially sad to notice the three things phase II offered that no other Leysdown arcade offered had been removed: The Laser quest, 'fun factory' and bumper cars have all been demolished. A new bowling alley has been put in its place however, as well as the bingo being built too. Hope fully with Jimmy owning several other arcades too, he will be able to bring a new lease of life to Leysdown, as I'm sure many people would would agree, it could definitely do with a good renovation. / Jimmy Godden / Jimmy Godden is known as the 'King of the South-Coast', owning various different arcades throughout sea-side towns in the South East of England. info_text: Trampoline centre with arcade machines. Some arcade machines are in the cafe and some are in a separate dedicated area/alcove. Either way, it's not stated as being necessary to sign up for a trampolining session to access the machines. Having said that, at least one ziv contributor was prevented from accessing the arcade area due to not having a booking and was informed by the manager that you need to either have a booking or be accompanying someone with a booking to be allowed to walk to the area where the arcade machines are located. / Also, if you don't have a booking, you can't access the O2 itself before it officially opens at 10am and therefore can't access the arcade machines. For example on Saturdays, Oxygen Freejumping nominally opens at 9am and the O2 officially opens at 10am. So if you arrive between 9 and 10, you can't get to the arcade area unless you have a trampolining booking, as O2 security will prevent you from entering the O2 itself. (After 10am you won't have this problem.) Because of this, listed the opening time as 10am each day rather than what it says on the Oxygen website. / In addition to the listed games, there are a few sweet machines: / *Chupa Chups...
